key_insight: AlB12–Al detonation coatings improved the wear resistance of steel 45, with AB70 showing stable tribological behavior across the tested friction conditions.
engineering_relevance: These coatings offer a potential surface-engineering route for improving the durability of steel components exposed to sliding wear.
method: Deposit AB70 (AlB12–30 wt.% Al) and AB30 (AlB12–70 wt.% Al) using a DNEPR-5M detonation-spray system.
Evaluate coating properties and tribological behavior under varying sliding speeds and loads.
Examine post-friction surface structures to identify wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 170–200 μm coating thickness and, for AB70, friction coefficients of 0.21–0.38 and wear rates of 3.3–8.6 μm/km, with coated samples outperforming uncoated steel 45.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify test loads, sliding speeds, or statistical uncertainty, limiting assessment of performance under service conditions.
paper_title: Structure and properties of AlB12-Al detonation coatings on steel 45
